question: How do web browsers use Hyperlinks?

options.text: To navigate between web pages and resources

solution:
The correct answer is __**To navigate between web pages and resources**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Web page** is often accessed and displayed on a monitor or mobile device through an online browser. 
 
• A **hyperlink **points to a whole document or to a specific element within a document.
 
• A **hyperlink **helps the user traverse between different objects when the user hovers over it or clicks on it. It can be added by using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+K.
 
• When the user activates the link (e.g., by clicking on it with the mouse) the browser displays the link's target. If the target is not an HTML file, depending on the file type and on the browser and its plugins, another program may be activated to open the file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• URL: The URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. A URL is used for determining the address of a given distinctive resource online. In theory, every valid universal resource locator points to a novel resource. Such resources may be a Hypertext Markup Language page, a CSS document, an image, etc.
 
• Web page: A web page may be a document for the World Wide Web that's known by a novel uniform resource surveyor (URL). A Web page is often accessed and displayed on a monitor or mobile device through an online browser. The information found on a very website is sometimes in a markup language or XHTML format. The online pages sometimes additionally contain alternative resources like text, graphics, audio, video, sheets, scripts and pictures for multi-purpose usage. Users are also ready to navigate to alternative pages through machine-readable text links.
 
• Browser: A web browser is an application software package for accessing websites. Once a user requests a web page from a selected website, the browser retrieves its files from the Internet by using the web server and displays the page on the user's screen. Browsers are used on a spread of devices, together with desktops, laptops, tablets, and smartphones. Google Chrome, Safari and Firefox are examples of web browsers.
